clue.text: Succeeded after hard line taken with drug in Athenian Olympic events

indicators.note: after says the letter for succeeded is placed behind the rest
the three pieces taken together go inside the word for Athenian, splitting it open

parts.note: Attic means of Athens, ancient Attica's city
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A doped athlete, caught with a drug after taking a hard line, wins at the Athens Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athenian' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies ATTIC; 'taken with' is just a link joining H and L to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletics is the collective name for the track and field disciplines contested at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: A drunkard seen around clubs in Berkshire town

indicators.note: the drunkard's word goes around the letter for clubs

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A drunk is spotted visiting nightclubs in a Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a Berkshire town famed for its royal racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a town in the English county of Berkshire, home of the famous racecourse.

clue.text: Sure to hear mix-up about son being kept in

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the letter for son
a mix-up is a confusion, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A son, confined to his room, has trouble making himself heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix-up' scrambles SURE TO HEAR into HOUEARREST, which goes 'about' S.
explanation.definitionFit: House arrest is confinement to one's own home by authority, being kept indoors.

clue.text: Pride misplaced after English ten got run out

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters come behind the English and ten pieces

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer's pride is hurt when the England team, ten down, is run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, but 'run out' is the definition: expired. 'misplaced' rearranges PRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Expired means come to an end or lapsed, as a licence or time limit that has run out.

clue.text: Cruel and silly to bring in bad smell

indicators.note: the silly word brings the smell word inside itself

parts.note: inane means silly or senseless
hum is British slang for an unpleasant smell

explanation.surface: It is cruel and pointless to bring a stink into the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane means lacking compassion, causing needless suffering, a straightforward synonym for cruel.

clue.text: Writer's papers needing sorting out

definitions.note: writer is; the 's links definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the papers need putting in order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author's untidy pile of papers needs tidying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sapper' was the pen name of H. C. McNeile, creator of Bulldog Drummond; a sapper is also a military engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapper was the pseudonym of the British novelist Herman Cyril McNeile, author of the Bulldog Drummond stories.

clue.text: Wanders right away — or doesn't?

definitions.note: short for doesn't wander, a verb phrase matching the third-person verb

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for right is sent off from the word for wanders

parts.note: strays means wanders off

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone drifts off or remains put.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the first half: 'doesn't' means doesn't wander, i.e. remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain in place is the opposite of wandering off, so someone who doesn't roam remains.

clue.text: Left in to cook gently with less fat

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the cooking word

parts.note: to simmer is to cook just below the boil

explanation.surface: A healthy recipe says leave it in to cook gently to reduce the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimmer, the comparative of slim, means thinner, carrying less body fat.

clue.text: Go further ahead designing shows

indicators.note: the two words show, display, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Moving forward with a design reveals more.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to put more on, to extend something, going further than before.

clue.text: City blue player wears, pulled over chest

indicators.note: the blue word wears, puts on around itself, the rest

parts.note: sad means blue, low in spirits

indicators.note: the player is pulled over, wrapped round, the chest like a jumper

parts.note: a man is a player or piece in chess and board games
an ark is a chest or box, as the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A Manchester City footballer, wearing blue, pulls a jumper over his chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' and 'blue' suggest Manchester City's kit, but City is the definition: Samarkand in Uzbekistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand is an ancient city on the Silk Road, now in Uzbekistan.

clue.text: Foolish person puts pressure on close friend

indicators.note: in an across answer, putting one piece on another means placing it after it

parts.note: a chum is a close friend
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A fool leans on his best mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump is a British informal word for a silly or gullible person, a fool.

clue.text: Joint I'm rolling with dope? This may be my thing

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body

indicators.note: rolling suggests the letters are turned over and mixed up, as a joint is rolled

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rolling a joint of cannabis declares it is just their scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' and 'dope' suggest cannabis, but the joint is the hip; 'rolling' rearranges I'M and DOPE into PIEDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing your own thing was a catchphrase of the hippy world, so hippiedom is where that phrase belongs.

clue.text: Sort of key on a particular brass instrument providing volume

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the trumpet, with the definite article, is one particular brass instrument
major is one kind of musical key, alongside minor

explanation.surface: A musician tunes a trumpet in a certain key so it plays loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' looks like loudness in a musical scene, but it means a book: Thomas Hardy's novel of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume is a book, and this title is a novel by Thomas Hardy set in Dorset during the Napoleonic wars.

clue.text: Play one's found no longer moving at this point

definitions.meaning: R. C. Sherriff's 1928 First World War drama

definitions.text: one's found no longer moving at this point
definitions.meaning: the destination where a traveller comes to rest

explanation.surface: In a theatre piece, the travellers stop moving here.
explanation.definitionFit: It names Sherriff's trench drama and also the place where a trip ends and movement stops.

clue.text: Urgent weapons, the last to get to the front

indicators.text: the last to get to the front
indicators.note: the final letter of the weapons word is shifted to the very start

parts.note: tridents are three-pronged spears

explanation.surface: Pressing weapons where the rearguard is sent to the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and forceful, insistently pressing, close in sense to urgent.

clue.text: One who has left politics

parts.note: reads as a retired politician, but means someone whose political views are left-wing

explanation.definitionFit: A believer in left-wing politics, holding views of public ownership and equality, is the person described.

clue.text: US president mostly circumventing a physical injury

indicators.note: circumventing means going around, so the shortened name wraps round the A
mostly means all but the last letter of the president's name

parts.note: Harry Truman was the 33rd US president

explanation.surface: A US president nearly gets round a bodily injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma in medicine is a physical wound or bodily injury, as in a trauma unit.

clue.text: Having lost Villa fixture — not that important

parts.note: a home fixture is a match on one's own ground
less means lesser, of smaller importance

explanation.surface: Losing to Aston Villa in a match that mattered little.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club, but here villa means a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lost their villa, their house, is left without a home.

clue.text: A big one would be important in Caerphilly

definitions.text: A big one would be important in Caerphilly

parts.words: A big one would be important in Caerphilly
parts.note: an important person is a big ___, and in the Welsh town of Caerphilly, which gives its name to a crumbly white variety, the dairy product itself matters

explanation.walkthrough: Caerphilly is a town in South Wales and a crumbly white cheese named after it; a 'big cheese' is an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is a VIP, and Caerphilly is a well-known British variety of this dairy food.

clue.text: Interim stretch between two sentences?

definitions.meaning: a temporary measure filling in until something permanent arrives
playfully read as the space after a full stop

explanation.surface: A temporary period between two prison terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary substitute, and whimsically the space following a full stop.

clue.text: Prisoner's punished, being locked up

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner; the 's is a link meaning is
fined means punished with a money penalty

explanation.surface: A convict is penalised while serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: Confined means shut in or imprisoned, the state of someone kept under lock and key.

clue.text: Refrain from ball in dread

indicators.note: in puts the ball word inside the dread word

parts.note: fear means dread
an orb is a sphere or ball

explanation.surface: Avoiding a ball out of terror.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to hold back from doing something, the same as to refrain from it.

clue.text: Higher price offered, we hear, showing unhealthy interest

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are spoken and matched by sound

parts.note: a higher price offered at auction is a more bid

explanation.surface: A higher auction offer, it seems, reveals an unhealthy fascination.
explanation.definitionFit: Morbid means having an abnormal fascination with death and gloomy subjects.

clue.text: So no roar at M. Ryle's becoming this?

definitions.text: So no roar at M. Ryle's becoming this?
definitions.note: Sir Martin Ryle, Nobel-winning radio astronomer, held the Crown's top astronomical post from 1972

indicators.note: becoming signals that the preceding words turn into something else, a new arrangement

parts.note: the initial taken as written
the name taken as written; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: Asks whether there was no fanfare when the radio astronomer Martin Ryle took up a royal post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges SO NO ROAR AT M RYLE; the whole clue also defines, since Martin Ryle was appointed to the post in 1972.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Ryle actually held this honorary post, the monarch's chief astronomer, from 1972 to 1982.

clue.text: Composer announcing items on the programme

indicators.note: announcing means saying out, so the words are matched by what is spoken

parts.note: a programme lists items, so lists are items on it

explanation.surface: A composer is announced among the evening's listed pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and virtuoso pianist.

clue.text: Will beg Bible not to be opened — it's unreadable

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its opening letter, as if left unopened

explanation.surface: A will asks that the family Bible stay closed, being indecipherable anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to be opened' removes the first letters W, B and B from Will, beg and Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegible describes writing too poor or faded to be read, which is exactly what unreadable means.

clue.text: Record containing artist's introduction once about the track

indicators.note: the record holds the artist's first letter inside it

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so the first letter of the artist's name

explanation.surface: An LP with the artist's opening track on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' joins 'about the track' to define: one circuit round a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap is one full circuit, going round a running track a single time.

clue.text: Man's losing the way — it's a straight bet

indicators.note: losing tells us letters go missing from the man's name

parts.note: Steven's, a man's name with its possessive, gives these letters
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A man who has lost his route places a simple wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' stands for any man's name, here STEVEN'S; dropping ST, short for street, leaves the bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens are odds of one to one, an even-money bet with no handicap, a straightforward wager.

clue.text: It's a plus to give birth

parts.note: taken as written
to pup is to give birth, as a seal or dog does

explanation.surface: Having a baby is a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up is an additional amount added to fill something up, an extra or plus.

clue.text: Doubt harm done to reputation

definitions.meaning: to doubt a claim is to refuse it credence, a verb sense
loss of good name or standing, the noun sense

explanation.surface: Being doubted is damaging to one's good name.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cast doubt on; as a noun it means disgrace or loss of standing.
